Header:
Date: 2025-10-15
Start time (UTC): 09:23
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM), Mark Liu (Aurora GC), Jenna Park (Aurora Procurement), Raj Patel (Aurora CTO), Samir Khan (Aurora Security), Speaker 1 (Aurora intern)
Recording id: ff-2025-10-15-aurora-msa-dpa-0923

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Quick procurement/legal sync to review MSA and DPA items, clarify SLAs and data residency/KMS needs, finalize pricing approval steps and vendor onboarding checklist. Action items include Redwood sending redlines and security artifacts; Aurora to confirm procurement timeline.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA data retention, SLA and uptime commitments, SOC 2/ISO references, private deployment vs hosted, pricing approval flow, onboarding runbook, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. We're gonna go through the MSA and DPA notes and then hit the onboarding and pricing steps. Priya and Diego are here from the team. Quick intro?
[00:08] Priya Shah: Hi all, Priya, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll handle the technical bits and the onboarding checklist later.
[00:13] Mark Liu: Mark Liu, general counsel at Aurora. I'll be leading the legal redline discussion.
[00:17] Jenna Park: Jenna, procurement. I'll focus on the PO and approval timeline.
[00:20] Raj Patel: Raj, CTO. I care about deployment options, latency, and any network constraints.
[00:24] Samir Khan: Samir, head of security, I'll cover compliance and key mgmt.
[00:27] Speaker 1: Thanks.
[00:30] Alex Mercer: Great. Quick agenda: legal redlines, DPA specifics, SLAs, pricing approval timeline, then tech onboarding notes. If we run over we'll follow-up.
[00:40] Mark Liu: Cool. On the MSA we've got a few items: indemnity carveouts, data processing terms, and termination for convenience notice period. Also, the auto-renew clause we want to tighten.
[00:52] Alex Mercer: Sure, we can discuss each. On indemnity, our standard is limited; can you confirm the scope you're looking for?
[00:58] Mark Liu: We're pushing for third-party IP claims to be more explicit and a mutual cap on liability tied to fees — or a negotiated cap if possible.
[01:07] Priya Shah: Just to flag, in cases where customers ask for higher caps, that usually routes to legal Ops and may hit executive sign-off. AE can escalate.
[01:15] Diego Ramos: Yeah, and for high-risk pockets we do have enterprise amendments.
[01:20] Jenna Park: From procurement, we need the MSA redlines in Word so we can mark them in DocuSign flow. PDF is fine but Word preferred.
[01:27] Alex Mercer: We'll send Word. Mark, we'll include a proposed liability cap and note where deviations require approval.
[01:34] Mark Liu: Good. DPA: data residency — Aurora requires EU data residency for EU customer data and strict deletion policies after 90 days for PII used in evals.
[01:46] Samir Khan: Also require KMS integration with our HSM. We can't have keys stored in a foreign-managed KMS. We want CMK in our cloud KMS and HSM-backed if possible.
[01:56] Priya Shah: We support customer-managed KMS for dedicated/private deployments — can be integrated. For hosted, we do offer bring-your-own-key patterns, but there are architectural notes — the KV cache and ephemeral inference keys flow might still be handled by Redwood. I'll share the exact diagram.
[02:11] Raj Patel: For private deployment, what's the SLA difference? Can you summarize hosted vs dedicated vs private in terms of uptime and support?
[02:19] Alex Mercer: Hosted API standard SLA is 99.9% API availability; Dedicated gets 99.95 and higher with reserved capacity. Private is negotiable — it depends on the on-prem infra runbook but we provide support SLAs in the enterprise contract.
[02:32] Mark Liu: We also need an audit log retention guarantee — 1 year at minimum, preferably 2.
[02:39] Diego Ramos: Audit logs retention is configurable; default retention for hosted is 12 months, can extend as an add-on. We'll note that in the DPA options.
[02:47] Alex Mercer: For SOC 2, we have our report and ISO 27001 cert, we'll attach those.
[02:52] Jenna Park: Great, that'll help procurement. 
[02:55] Mark Liu: Back to DPA — processor/subprocessor list. We need a complete PaaS/subproc list with hosting regions. Some subproc names in your template are ambiguous — e.g., 'CDN provider' — we need specific vendor names.
[03:08] Priya Shah: Understood, we'll produce a subprocessor list with vendor names and regions.
[03:12] Samir Khan: For encryption in transit, we want TLS 1.2 minimum, ideally 1.3, and agreed ciphers. Also FIPS-140 validated HSM for key storage.
[03:22] Priya Shah: Yes TLS 1.3 supported; we can share the cipher list. For keys we integrate with customer KMS and HSMs depending on deployment.
[03:29] Raj Patel: Network wise, do you support VPC peering, private link, or just VPN? We prefer VPC peering to avoid hairpin routing.
[03:38] Priya Shah: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink depending on cloud provider and region; we'll include the terraform snippet in the onboarding pack.
[03:45] Jenna Park: On pricing, finance needs a finalized worksheet. We had the tiered committed capacity numbers — is that still your best offer?
[03:53] Alex Mercer: The committed capacity quote we sent stands: three tiers with discounts at 6- and 12-month commits. There was also an optional dedicated pool for the high-throughput models. We can lock pricing for a 30-day approval window if that helps.
[04:06] Jenna Park: Locking for 30 days is good. We need to route to legal and then finance for PO. Our internal approvals usually take 7-10 business days after legal sign-off.
[04:15] Mark Liu: One more legal item: termination for convenience notice — we want 60 days rather than 30. Any concerns?
[04:22] Alex Mercer: We can consider 60 days on dedicated or private, but on hosted it may be 30 due to resource reallocation. We can flag it as a negotiable clause.
[04:32] Mark Liu: Okay. Liability cap again — suggest 12 months of fees or a dollar amount.
[04:38] Diego Ramos: Standard is 12 months of fees for similar deals; enterprise can negotiate higher with ARR thresholds.
[04:44] Raj Patel: On SLAs, do you have credits or financial remedies? We need specifics in the SLA section — e.g., credits scaling at 0.1% of monthly fee per 0.1% below target.
[04:56] Alex Mercer: We do service credits, details in the SLA clause. We'll surface the exact formula in the redline.
[05:03] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[05:06] Mark Liu: Can we also confirm data deletion proof? After termination we want an attestation and evidence of deletion within X days.
[05:15] Priya Shah: We provide deletion attestations for enterprise/private. For hosted, we can provide logs and deletion confirmation within 30 days, and for private we can provide runbook evidence.
[05:25] Samir Khan: Ok, also need a security questionnaire — CAIQ and our vendor risk team will run a 3rd party scan. Can you complete the CAIQ?
[05:33] Alex Mercer: Yes, we'll complete the CAIQ and share our penetration test summary and SOC 2.
[05:38] Jenna Park: Regarding onboarding, what's the expected timeline from signed agreement to production? We're aiming for a phased pilot in 6 weeks.
[05:46] Priya Shah: For a hosted pilot, we can onboard in 1-2 weeks. For dedicated it's usually 4-6 weeks depending on capacity and networking. Private/on-prem can be 8-12 weeks. A 6-week phased pilot for dedicated is achievable if network approvals move quickly.
[05:59] Raj Patel: Good. For the pilot we want an isolated environment and data segregation from other customers.
[06:05] Diego Ramos: Dedicated pools give that isolation; private is complete control. We'll document options.
[06:10] Mark Liu: One more procurement item — invoice and payment terms: Net 45 or Net 30? Aurora's policy tends to be Net 45 for new vendors. Any flexibility?
[06:18] Alex Mercer: Standard is Net 30; enterprise contracts can accommodate Net 45 with a small fee or annual prepay option. We'll note that as negotiable.
[06:27] Jenna Park: We'll capture that in the pricing sheet discussion.
[06:30] Alex Mercer: Let's pivot to the DPA specifics — retention windows, subprocessor notifications, breach notification windows (we usually do 72 hours).
[06:39] Mark Liu: 72 hours is acceptable; we want immediate notification for any exfiltration. Also SLA on forensic support — we need cooperation clauses.
[06:47] Priya Shah: Forensic support is available in enterprise packs; we'll include response times for initial triage and deeper forensics.
[06:55] Samir Khan: Also, log access — we need a way to access audit logs for our customers on demand.
[07:01] Priya Shah: We can provide log exports and role-based access; Redwood Console supports per-route dashboards and audit exports.
[07:08] Raj Patel: Do you encrypt at rest and in transit by default?
[07:12] Priya Shah: Yes, TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest; for CMK we integrate with customer KMS.
[07:18] Mark Liu: About the subproc list — please provide a 3rd-party vendor contact for each.
[07:23] Alex Mercer: We'll include vendor contacts.
[07:26] Jenna Park: On the pricing approval path — who in Redwood will own quoting updates? We need a single point of contact to move paperwork.
[07:34] Alex Mercer: That's me, Alex. I'll be the PO point. I'll loop finance if adjustments needed.
[07:39] Jenna Park: Good. We'll submit the procurement sheet once we receive the redlined MSA and the SOC 2.
[07:45] Mark Liu: For the DPA, can you confirm deletion periods for backups? That's often sticky.
[07:51] Priya Shah: Backups retention varies; for hosted default backups are retained 30 days, but we can offer shorter/longer retention on enterprise plans and private. We'll call that out in the DPA.
[08:03] Raj Patel: Technical question, Priya: how do you handle model updates and version pinning? We need guaranteed inference model version for the pilot.
[08:11] Priya Shah: You can pin model versions per route; we support rollouts and can freeze model version for pilot. Automatic updates only if you opt-in.
[08:19] Raj Patel: How about KV cache persistence across restarts?
[08:23] Priya Shah: KV cache is in-memory for latency; we have optional persistent cache layers for private/dedicated if you need warm starts. We'll include configuration notes.
[08:33] Mark Liu: One administrative: can you produce a master services clause with an appendix for dedicated privacy addendum? We prefer modular docs.
[08:41] Alex Mercer: Absolutely, modular MSAs with addenda is our standard. We'll deliver MSA + DPA + SLA appendix.
[08:49] Diego Ramos: Also, we'll include an onboarding runbook link: short URL will be in the follow-up.
[08:55] Jenna Park: For signatures, do you support DocuSign and offline sign? We need to know the flow.
[08:59] Alex Mercer: DocuSign is supported. We can also do manual signature workflow for legal if needed.
[09:05] Mark Liu: Ok good. A few quick clarifying questions: are there penalties for data residency breach? We need remediation clauses.
[09:12] Alex Mercer: We don't have automatic monetary penalties for residency breaches; remediation / cure periods and contractual remedies are standard — we can discuss specific remedies in the redline.
[09:22] Samir Khan: Also an escrow for model weights? Not required currently but asking.
[09:27] Priya Shah: Model weights are managed by Redwood; we don't typically escrow weights, but we can discuss options for long-term commitments.
[09:34] Jenna Park: Back on procurement timing — once we have the redline and SOC2, we'll need 3 internal approvals: Legal, Security, Finance. That should be a 7-10 business day window.
[09:44] Alex Mercer: Noted. We'll aim to get redlines to you by Friday (2025-10-17).
[09:48] Mark Liu: Great. Any other items?
[09:50] Raj Patel: Just to confirm testing — can we run a short perf benchmark with our sample workload? Network egress numbers etc.
[09:58] Priya Shah: Yes, Priya: will run a benchmark. We'll need a sample prompt set and expected QPS; we can run it on hosted or dedicated as a pre-production run.
[10:08] Alex Mercer: We'll coordinate that in the onboarding pack.
[10:11] Diego Ramos: I'll include contact for billing ops and the engineer assigned for the pilot.
[10:17] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[10:20] Jenna Park: Thanks everyone. Recap?
[10:22] Alex Mercer: Recap: Redwood sends redlined MSA+DPA+SLA, SOC 2 & ISO cert, subprocessor list, CAIQ, onboarding runbook, terraform snippets, and sample network diagram by 2025-10-17/20. Aurora to confirm procurement timeline and provide sample workload for benchmarking. We'll schedule an exec summary call 2025-10-22.
[10:40] Mark Liu: That works.
[10:42] Samir Khan: We'll send required cipher list and KMS requirements by Monday.
[10:46] Jenna Park: We'll aim to get internal approvals within 10 business days after receiving redlines.
[10:50] Alex Mercer: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the documents and next steps.
[10:55] Raj Patel: Appreciate it.
[10:58] Alex Mercer: End.

Notes: timestamps approximate. Transcript contains occasional filler and mis-attributions. References to product names sometimes generic (e.g., KV cache spelled as 'K-V cache' in audio).
